claim: scMOCa permits labeling cells of interest by attaching streptavidin-coated magnetic beads to their membranes using the lasers of a confocal microscope.
source: Here, we present a new method that permits labeling cells of interest by attaching streptavidin-coated magnetic beads to their membranes using the lasers of a confocal microscope.
evidence: The abstract directly states this as a key feature of the method, and the manuscript provides detailed protocols and images demonstrating this process.

claim: A simple magnet allows highly specific isolation of labeled cells using scMOCa.
source: A simple magnet allows highly specific isolation of the labeled cells, which then remain viable and proliferate normally.
evidence: The abstract states this claim, and experimental data in Figures 2 and 3 demonstrate high specificity of cell isolation.

claim: Cells isolated using scMOCa remain viable and proliferate normally.
source: A simple magnet allows highly specific isolation of the labeled cells, which then remain viable and proliferate normally.
evidence: The abstract makes this claim, and Figure 4 shows multiple cell types proliferating normally after sorting.

claim: scMOCa can isolate individual cells based on the presence of multiple nuclei.
source: As proof of principle, we tagged, isolated, and expanded individual cells based on three biologically relevant visual characteristics: i) presence of multiple nuclei, ii) accumulation of lipid vesicles, and iii) ability to resolve ionizing radiation-induced DNA damage foci.
evidence: The abstract lists this as one of three proof-of-principle applications, and Figure 6 shows multinucleated cells isolated and cultured.

claim: scMOCa can isolate individual cells based on accumulation of lipid vesicles.
source: As proof of principle, we tagged, isolated, and expanded individual cells based on three biologically relevant visual characteristics: i) presence of multiple nuclei, ii) accumulation of lipid vesicles, and iii) ability to resolve ionizing radiation-induced DNA damage foci.
evidence: The abstract lists this as one of three proof-of-principle applications, and Figure 6E-F shows differentiated adipocytes with lipid vesicles isolated and cultured.

claim: scMOCa can isolate individual cells based on their ability to resolve ionizing radiation-induced DNA damage foci.
source: As proof of principle, we tagged, isolated, and expanded individual cells based on three biologically relevant visual characteristics: i) presence of multiple nuclei, ii) accumulation of lipid vesicles, and iii) ability to resolve ionizing radiation-induced DNA damage foci.
evidence: The abstract lists this as one of three proof-of-principle applications, and Figure 5 demonstrates isolation and characterization of cells with fast 53BP1 focus resolution.

claim: Cell migration is an essential determinant in normal embryonic development, wound healing, immune responses, tumor progression, and vascular disease.
source: For example, cell migration (movement) is an essential determinant in normal embryonic development, wound healing, immune responses, tumor progression, and vascular disease (Kurosaka and Kashina, 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Kurosaka and Kashina, 2008.

claim: Changes in cellular morphology constitute biomarkers of cellular growth, division, death, and differentiation, as well as of tissue morphogenesis and disease.
source: Moreover, changes in cellular morphology (shape) constitute biomarkers of cellular growth, division, death, and differentiation, as well as of tissue morphogenesis and disease (Prasad and Alizadeh, 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Prasad and Alizadeh, 2019.

claim: Cell-to-cell contacts or distance to sources of chemical cues are critical factors in chemokinesis, differentiation, neural function, and immune responses.
source: Cell-to-cell contacts (location) or distance to sources of chemical cues such as senescent cells, inflammation or necrotic tissue are critical factors in chemokinesis, differentiation, neural function, and immune responses (Garcia et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Garcia et al., 2018.

claim: Cell Labeling via Photobleaching (CLaP) allows arbitrary tagging of individual cells among a heterogeneous population by crosslinking biotin molecules to their plasma membranes with confocal microscope lasers.
source: We recently developed a method termed Cell Labeling via Photobleaching (CLaP) (Binan et al., 2016) allowing the arbitrary tagging of individual cells among a heterogeneous population within a microscopy field. This is accomplished by crosslinking biotin molecules to their plasma membranes with the lasers of a confocal microscope, followed by use of fluorescent streptavidin conjugates to reveal the marked cells.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Binan et al., 2016 and describes a previously developed method.

claim: CLaP does not require previous knowledge of surface markers or transfection of reporter genes.
source: In this manner, the same instrument used for imaging can also be adapted to label particular cells based on any visible trait that distinguishes them from the ensemble. Importantly, previous knowledge of surface markers or transfection of reporter genes are not required.
evidence: This claim is stated in the introduction and is supported by the citation to Binan et al., 2016.

claim: The CLaP label is stable, non-toxic, retained in cells for several days, and does not engender detectable changes in cell morphology, viability, or proliferative capacity.
source: The mark is stable, non-toxic, retained in cells for several days, and moreover, does not engender detectable changes in cell morphology, viability, or proliferative capacity.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Binan et al., 2016.

claim: Gene expression profiling indicated no major changes associated with the CLaP procedure.
source: Moreover, gene expression profiling indicated no major changes associated with the procedure (Binan et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Binan et al., 2016.

claim: Classical protocols like FACS and MACS are typically optimized for high throughput at the expense of capture efficiency and specificity, and require large numbers of cells.
source: However, as mentioned above, current sorting techniques cannot efficiently isolate such rare cells (Pappas and Wang, 2007); indeed, classical protocols like Fluorescence and Magnetic Activated Cell Sorting (FACS and MACS) are typically optimized for high throughput at the expense of capture efficiency and specificity, and require large numbers of cells (Pappas and Wang, 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Pappas and Wang, 2007.

claim: Small cell populations representing 10−3 of the total have been defined as rare, or ultrarare in the case of 10−5.
source: Small cell populations representing 10−3 of the total, which have been defined as rare, or ultrarare in the case of 10−5, can only be effectively captured and purified with repeated cycles of sorting and cell expansion protocols (Pappas and Wang, 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Pappas and Wang, 2007.

claim: Rare cell populations can only be effectively captured and purified with repeated cycles of sorting and cell expansion protocols.
source: Small cell populations representing 10−3 of the total, which have been defined as rare, or ultrarare in the case of 10−5, can only be effectively captured and purified with repeated cycles of sorting and cell expansion protocols (Pappas and Wang, 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Pappas and Wang, 2007.

claim: Highly conservative gating strategies for rare cell populations can at best achieve approximately 45% purity.
source: Starting with rare and hence precious cell populations, highly conservative gating strategies are needed, which can at best achieve approximately 45% purity (Kuka, 2013; Shields et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Kuka, 2013 and Shields et al., 2015.

claim: Time-consuming manipulations, cost, hardware footprint, and handling complexity make approaches based on microfluidics ill-suited for capturing small numbers of cells.
source: Time-consuming manipulations, cost, hardware footprint, and handling complexity (Takahashi and Okada, 1970) make approaches based on microfluidics ill-suited for capturing small numbers of cells, which are often masked within tens of thousands.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Takahashi and Okada, 1970.

claim: The biotin-streptavidin bond has a dissociation constant (Kd) of 10−15M.
source: The high strength of the biotin streptavidin bond (Kd = 10−15M) allows stringent rinsing and efficient removal of unbound magnetic beads, which is key to obtaining specific tagging allowed by the accurate laser pointing (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is a well-established biochemical property stated in the manuscript.

claim: Depending on their size, beads may be internalized (nanometer-size beads) or retained at the cell surface and shared between daughter cells after mitosis (micron-size beads).
source: Depending on their size, beads may later be internalized (nanometer-size beads), or retained at the cell surface and shared between daughter cells after mitosis (micron-size beads).
evidence: This is stated as an observation about bead behavior in the manuscript.

claim: Special beads with a DNA spacer between streptavidin and magnetic core allow enzymatic cleavage for detachment from cells.
source: If needed, special beads, which integrate a DNA spacer between the streptavidin and their magnetic core to allow enzymatic cleavage, are commercially available (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and demonstrated in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: scMOCa achieves high capture efficiency, with a linear fit of capture data yielding a slope of 0.99.
source: A linear fit of the data yielded a slope of 0.99, demonstrating that scMOCa is highly efficient in retrieving all target cells, after testing 1 to 50 cells.
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Out of 23 experiments starting from samples of 50,000 cells, the largest deviation from perfect recovery was one test where only 3 instead of 5 positive cells were captured.
source: Out of 23 experiments, starting from samples of 50,000 cells, the largest deviation from perfect recovery corresponds to one test where only 3, instead of 5 positive cells, were captured (two positive cells lost).
evidence: This is a direct statement of experimental results.

claim: scMOCa can isolate cells with five-orders-of-magnitude enrichment, generating pure samples from a rare cell population representing 0.02% of the total.
source: Our examples represent a five-orders-of-magnitude enrichment, as pure samples originating from a rare cell population (0.02% of the total) can be generated.
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by the PCR data in Figure 3B-C showing pure dog cell samples isolated from a mixed population.

claim: Commercial MACS columns isolated 5.3 ± 1.5 positive cells on average while also capturing 17.6 ± 7.3 negative cells in three independent experiments attempting to isolate 30 tagged cells from 30,000.
source: In three independent experiments, we could isolate 5.3 ± 1.5 positive cells on average, while also capturing 17.6 ± 7.3 negative cells.
evidence: This is a direct statement of experimental results comparing scMOCa to commercial methods.

claim: Using commercial MACS columns, approximately 75% of captured cells were contaminating false-positive cells with no beads attached.
source: This represents a population in which approximately 75% of the captured cells are contaminating false-positive cells with no beads attached, while scMOCa generates pure samples (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is stated as a result of the comparison experiment with commercial MACS columns.

claim: After scMOCa sorting, cells are initially round after trypsin treatment but display normal elongated shapes after one day in culture.
source: Immediately after capture cells are round (as expected after trypsin treatment), but after one day in culture they display normal elongated shapes (Figure 4).
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by images in Figure 4.

claim: Upon proliferation after scMOCa sorting, the number of cells with beads attached is reduced exponentially as cells divide.
source: Upon proliferation the number of cells with beads attached is reduced exponentially as cells divide (Figure 4, right panels).
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by images in Figure 4.

claim: scMOCa successfully sorted three different types of primary cells: human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVECs), human lung fibroblasts, and mouse dorsal root ganglion (DRG) neurons.
source: In addition to immortalized cell lines, we have tested and successfully sorted three different types of primary cells: human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVECs), human lung fibroblasts, and mice dorsal root ganglion (DRG) neurons dissected and plated 24 hr before the assay.
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by images in Figure 4.

claim: HUVECs and lung fibroblasts proliferated normally for several days after scMOCa sorting.
source: Importantly, HUVECs and lung fibroblasts proliferated normally for several days and primary DRG neurons actively extended cellular processes, as shown in Figure 4.
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by images in Figure 4.

claim: Primary DRG neurons actively extended cellular processes after scMOCa sorting.
source: Importantly, HUVECs and lung fibroblasts proliferated normally for several days and primary DRG neurons actively extended cellular processes, as shown in Figure 4.
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by images in Figure 4.

claim: Mouse embryonic stem cells sorted using scMOCa displayed similar growth and morphological features relative to the original population.
source: Finally, we tested mouse embryonic stem cells which, after capture and replating, displayed similar growth and morphological features relative to the original population.
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by images in Figure 4D.

claim: Sorted mouse embryonic stem cells migrated and regrouped into small colonies which proliferated normally during 10 days.
source: Indeed, cells sorted using gelatin-coated plastic chambers migrated and regrouped into small colonies which proliferated normally during 10 days.
evidence: This is a direct statement of experimental observations.

claim: Sorted mouse embryonic stem cells formed small poorly adherent spherical structures, which is expected as embryonic stem cells spontaneously form embryonic bodies in culture.
source: Sorted cells formed small poorly adherent spherical structures (Figure 4D) which is expected from embryonic stem cells as they are known to spontaneously form embryonic bodies in culture.
evidence: This claim combines experimental observation with established knowledge about embryonic stem cell behavior.

claim: Upon addition of 1 µM retinoic acid and removal of LIF, sorted mouse embryonic stem cells started differentiating during five additional days and became more adherent cells spread on the culture substrate.
source: Upon addition of 1 uM retinoic acid and removal of the leukemia inhibitory factor (LIF) from their medium, they started differentiating during five additional days (Figure 4D, right panel) and became more adherent cells spread on the culture substrate.
evidence: This is a direct statement of experimental results shown in Figure 4D.

claim: Conditioned medium can improve cell viability and proliferative potential at low cell numbers.
source: Cell viability and proliferative potential can be improved by the use of conditioned medium (Huang et al., 1990; Housden et al., 2015; Yamamoto et al., 2000), that is, medium collected from an exponentially growing cell culture and passed through a 0.2 µm filter.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Huang et al., 1990; Housden et al., 2015; and Yamamoto et al., 2000.

claim: Conditioned medium contains secreted factors that facilitate cell growth at very low density.
source: This is attributed to secreted factors that in turn facilitate cell growth at very low density (Huang et al., 1990; Yamamoto et al., 2000).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Huang et al., 1990 and Yamamoto et al., 2000.

claim: Collagen coating of the collection chamber can improve cell attachment and viability.
source: The top collection chamber can be coated with collagen to further improve cell attachment and viability (Fradet-Turcotte et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Fradet-Turcotte et al., 2013.

claim: 53BP1 is directly involved in DSB repair and is rapidly recruited to DSB sites where it forms foci that can be readily detected by fluorescence microscopy in live-cells when fused with GFP.
source: 53BP1 is directly involved in DSB repair and is rapidly recruited to DSB sites where it forms foci that can be readily detected by fluorescence microscopy in live-cells (Mirzayans et al., 2018) when fused with GFP.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Mirzayans et al., 2018.

claim: Foci of 53BP1 are resolved gradually as cells repair DSB, and within approximately 3 hr post-irradiation with 0.5 Gy most are expected to disappear.
source: Foci of 53BP1 are resolved gradually as cells repair DSB, and within approximately 3 hr post-irradiation with 0.5 Gy most are expected to disappear (Mirzayans et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Mirzayans et al., 2018.

claim: At 45 min post-irradiation with 0.5 Gy, an average of 10.2 ± 2.5 GFP-53BP1 foci per cell was detected in U2OS cells.
source: At 45 min post-irradiation an average of 10.2 ± 2.5 (mean ± standard deviation) foci per cell was detected.
evidence: This is a direct statement of experimental measurements.

claim: At 2 hr post-irradiation with 0.5 Gy, the average number of GFP-53BP1 foci in U2OS cells was reduced to 7.6 ± 2.3.
source: At 2 hr post-irradiation, a second set of images was acquired, and the average number of foci was reduced to 7.6 ± 2.3.
evidence: This is a direct statement of experimental measurements.

claim: On average, U2OS cells resolved approximately 25% of their 53BP1 foci within 2 hr after 0.5 Gy irradiation.
source: Since on average cells resolved approximately 25% of their foci within 2 hr, we defined cells in which more than 85% of foci have disappeared after 2 hr as 'fast resolving'.
evidence: This is stated as a result of the experimental measurements.

claim: Fast-resolving cells (those resolving more than 85% of foci within 2 hr) represented approximately 1% of the U2OS population.
source: Such fast resolving cells, represented approximately 1% of the population.
evidence: This is a direct statement of experimental observations.

claim: The average intensity of nuclei showed no correlation with the number of 53BP1 foci (Pearson coefficient of −0.15).
source: Indeed, we observed no change in global protein abundance or average intensity of GFP-53BP1 upon focus resolution: the average intensity of nuclei showed no correlation with the number of 53BP1 foci (Pearson coefficient of −0.15).
evidence: This is a direct statement of quantitative analysis results.

claim: FACS or similar approaches are not suitable for sorting based on focus resolution because the overall fluorescence signal originating from cell nuclei does not reflect the local distribution of protein.
source: We emphasize that FACS or similar approaches are not suitable for sorting based on focus resolution, even if the fraction of target cells was relatively large, as the overall fluorescence signal originating from cell nuclei does not reflect the local distribution of protein.
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by the Pearson coefficient data showing no correlation between average intensity and foci number.

claim: All three cell populations (parental and Populations #1 and #2) exhibited similar numbers of GFP-53BP1 foci per cell 45 min after irradiation.
source: Importantly, all three populations exhibited similar numbers of foci per cell 45 min after irradiation, indicating that the initial formation of 53BP1 foci is comparable between all cell populations.
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: The progeny of captured cells (Populations #1 and #2) retained the original visually detected phenotype of fast focus resolution.
source: However, we found that the progeny of captured cells (Populations #1 and #2) retained the original visually detected phenotype of fast focus resolution.
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 5B-C.

claim: Populations #1 and #2 resolved 53BP1 foci at least 1.5 times more rapidly than parental counterparts.
source: These cells resolved foci at least 1.5 times more rapidly than parental counterparts, as the median number of GFP-53BP1 foci per cell 60 min post-IR for Populations#1 and #2 (17 and 15 respectively) is equal to the median number of foci that parental cells exhibit at 90 min post-IR.
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: After 75 min post-irradiation, the numbers of foci in Populations #1 and #2 were statistically different from parental cells (p-values of 10−75 and 10−39 respectively).
source: After 75 min, these numbers of foci are already statistically different (p-values from student T-tests comparing the parental cells to Populations #1 and #2 are respectively 10−75 and 10−39).
evidence: This is a direct statement of statistical analysis results.

claim: No changes in the levels of either endogenous 53BP1 or GFP-tagged version were observed after irradiation.
source: To rule out the possibility that resolution of 53BP1 foci might be due to increased degradation upon IR or to globally decreased levels of the protein, we monitored 53BP1 levels by immunoblotting at different time points post-IR. No changes in the levels of either endogenous 53BP1 or GFP-tagged version was observed (Figure 5E).
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by immunoblot data shown in Figure 5E.

claim: All populations (parental and Populations #1 and #2) exhibit similar ratios of cells in each cell cycle phase.
source: Finally, FACS analysis shows that all populations exhibit similar ratios of cells in each cell cycle phase (Figure 5F).
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by FACS data shown in Figure 5F.

claim: The observed focus resolution differences between populations is unlikely to be attributable to cell cycle-related effects.
source: Therefore, the observed focus resolution differences between populations is unlikely to be attributable to cell cycle-related effects.
evidence: This is an inference based on the FACS data showing similar cell cycle distributions.

claim: Multinucleated cells constitute a rare subpopulation that does not express specific markers and cannot be differentiated from mononucleated polyploid cells using DNA-specific stains in a FACS experiment.
source: For example, multinucleated cells constitute a rare subpopulation (Mirzayans et al., 2017; Coward and Harding, 2014) that does not express specific markers and cannot be differentiated from mononucleated polyploid cells using DNA-specific stains in a FACS experiment.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Mirzayans et al., 2017 and Coward and Harding, 2014.

claim: Multinucleated cells can be easily identified visually even without DNA staining.
source: However, multinucleated cells can be easily identified visually even without DNA staining.
evidence: This is stated as an observation and is demonstrated by the images in Figure 6.

claim: Multinucleated cells have been described as generally being more aggressive and metastatic than mononucleated counterparts.
source: In the context of cancer, such cells have been (i) described as generally being more aggressive and metastatic than mononucleated counterparts, and (ii) proposed to be prone to acquisition of drug resistance and cancer relapse (Mirzayans et al., 2017; Mittal et al., 2017; Weihua et al., 2011; Green and Meuth, 1974).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Mirzayans et al., 2017; Mittal et al., 2017; Weihua et al., 2011; and Green and Meuth, 1974.

claim: Multinucleated cells have been proposed to be prone to acquisition of drug resistance and cancer relapse.
source: In the context of cancer, such cells have been (i) described as generally being more aggressive and metastatic than mononucleated counterparts, and (ii) proposed to be prone to acquisition of drug resistance and cancer relapse (Mirzayans et al., 2017; Mittal et al., 2017; Weihua et al., 2011; Green and Meuth, 1974).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Mirzayans et al., 2017; Mittal et al., 2017; Weihua et al., 2011; and Green and Meuth, 1974.

claim: Multinucleated cells can generate mononucleated progeny by budding.
source: Moreover, even though multinucleated cells do not undergo classical cytokinesis, they can generate mononucleated progeny by budding (Mirzayans et al., 2017; Weihua et al., 2011) and influence neighboring cells by secreting factors that promote stemness, as well as by transmitting sub-genomes (Mirzayans et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Mirzayans et al., 2017 and Weihua et al., 2011.

claim: Multinucleated cells can influence neighboring cells by secreting factors that promote stemness and by transmitting sub-genomes.
source: Moreover, even though multinucleated cells do not undergo classical cytokinesis, they can generate mononucleated progeny by budding (Mirzayans et al., 2017; Weihua et al., 2011) and influence neighboring cells by secreting factors that promote stemness, as well as by transmitting sub-genomes (Mirzayans et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Mirzayans et al., 2017.

claim: Multinucleated cells isolated using scMOCa remained viable for 4 days in culture.
source: Multinucleated cells were isolated using scMOCa and kept in culture for 4 days to evaluate their viability and metabolic activity (Figure 6).
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by images in Figure 6 showing viable cells with active mitochondria.

claim: scMOCa preserves the viability of isolated multinucleated cells, as indicated by Mitotracker staining of polarized mitochondrial membranes.
source: We used WGA-alexa647 to stain plasma membranes, and Hoechst for the nuclei (Figure 6) and Mitotracker green FM to tag polarized mitochondrial membranes, indicating that scMOCa preserves the viability of isolated cells (see Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by images in Figure 6 and Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: 3T3 cells are amongst the most common models to study metabolic disorders, for example, obesity.
source: These cells are amongst the most common models to study metabolic disorders, for example, obesity (Armani et al., 2010; Majka et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Armani et al., 2010 and Majka et al., 2014.

claim: When cultured for 2 days in medium containing dexamethasone, insulin and IBMX, and 3 days in medium containing insulin, a fraction of 3T3 cells differentiate and lipid vesicles accumulate in their cytoplasm.
source: When cultured for 2 days in medium containing dexamethasone, insulin and isobutylmethylxanthin (IBMX), an inhibitor of cyclic nucleotide phosphodiesterases, and 3 days in medium containing insulin, a fraction of 3T3 cells differentiate and lipid vesicles accumulate in their cytoplasm.
evidence: This is a direct statement of experimental protocol and observations.

claim: Flow cytometry sorting of adipocytes based on granularity requires several steps to select cells of interest and then remove false positives, such as debris and cell aggregates.
source: In order to obtain pure adipocyte cultures, flow cytometry sorting based on granularity requires several steps to select cells of interest and then remove false positives, such as debris and cell aggregates (Nagrath et al., 2007), whereas scMOCA may provide a much simpler approach to isolated live adipocytes, especially when these are present in very low abundance.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Nagrath et al., 2007.

claim: Sorted adipocytes remained viable and maintained their ability to store lipids in vesicles for a week after scMOCa capture.
source: We used scMOCA to capture differentiated adipocytes and then kept them in culture for a week (Figure 6). Sorted cells remained viable and maintained their ability to store lipids in vesicles that appear as clear spheres on Figure 6, while the magnetic beads that remained attached to cells membranes appear as dark spheres.
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and supported by images in Figure 6F.

claim: scMOCa is the only technology that permits isolation and subsequent clonal expansion of extremely small numbers of cells from relatively large heterogeneous populations based solely on visual criteria.
source: To the best of our knowledge, scMOCa is the only technology that permits isolation, and subsequent clonal expansion, of extremely small numbers of cells from relatively large heterogeneous populations based solely on visual criteria.
evidence: This is a claim about the uniqueness of the method based on the authors' knowledge of the field.

claim: FACS is not optimized for sorting rare cells.
source: The most widely used cell sorting technique, FACS, is not optimized for sorting rare cells.
evidence: This is stated as a limitation of FACS and is supported by the citation to Pappas and Wang, 2007.

claim: Adaptations needed for capturing cell populations representing <1% of the sample with high specificity make FACS experiments cumbersome and inefficient.
source: Adaptations needed for capturing cell populations representing <1% of the sample with high specificity make FACS experiments cumbersome and inefficient.
evidence: This is stated as a limitation of FACS.

claim: Repetition of flow cytometry sorting to obtain pure samples can only be performed with robust cell types due to reduced survival and proliferation capacity.
source: Moreover, repetition of flow cytometry sorting to obtain pure samples of a given cell type imposes can only be performed with robust cell types due to reduced survival and proliferation capacity (Pappas and Wang, 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Pappas and Wang, 2007.

claim: More refined procedures have been developed to sort rare cells via binding to microfluidic channels coated with antibodies against specific surface markers of interest.
source: More refined procedures have been developed to sort rare cells via binding to microfluidic channels coated with antibodies against specific surface markers of interest (Antfolk et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Antfolk et al., 2017.

claim: Microfluidic sorting requires high-affinity antibodies that are specific to the target cell types and leads to dilution of cells in laminar flows.
source: However, this requires high-affinity antibodies that are specific to the target cell types and leads to dilution of cells in laminar flows within microfluidics chips (Moon et al., 2011; Kang et al., 2012), which can become a drawback for downstream applications.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Moon et al., 2011 and Kang et al., 2012.

claim: Techniques based on magnetism display an improved capacity to isolate rare cells without dilution.
source: Techniques based on magnetism display an improved capacity to isolate rare cells without dilution (Tham et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Tham et al., 2014.

claim: The majority of protocols that use magnetic fields can capture cells of interest with efficiency near 90%, but their specificity remains a major challenge, with published results varying between 10% and 80% purity, generally closer to 50%.
source: Nevertheless, while the majority of protocols that use magnetic fields can capture cells of interest with efficiency near 90%, their specificity remains a major challenge, as published results vary between 10% and 80% purity for captured cells (Miltenyi et al., 1990), generally closer to 50% (Zborowski and Chalmers, 2011; Pamme and Wilhelm, 2006; Radbruch et al., 1994; Khojah et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Miltenyi et al., 1990; Zborowski and Chalmers, 2011; Pamme and Wilhelm, 2006; Radbruch et al., 1994; and Khojah et al., 2017.

claim: Only a handful of approaches allow label-free cell sorting, where intrinsic physical properties such as size or magnetic susceptibility differentiate the target population.
source: Finally, only a handful of approaches allow label-free cell sorting, where intrinsic physical properties, such as size (Zhao et al., 2017; Monti et al., 2017) or magnetic susceptibility (Moon et al., 2011; Pamme and Wilhelm, 2006; Hosokawa et al., 2010) differentiate the target population.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Zhao et al., 2017; Monti et al., 2017; Moon et al., 2011; Pamme and Wilhelm, 2006; and Hosokawa et al., 2010.

claim: Filtration relies on porous membranes to capture cells based on size and deformability and can achieve 80% efficiency.
source: Filtration, for example, relies on porous membranes to capture cells based on size and deformability (Davis et al., 2006; Gascoyne et al., 2009) and can achieve 80% efficiency.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Davis et al., 2006 and Gascoyne et al., 2009.

claim: Dielectrophoresis exploits natural differences in dielectric properties of cell types for discrimination and circulates cells in microfluidics channels, deviating target cells within an electric field.
source: Dielectrophoresis exploits natural differences in dielectric properties of cell types for discrimination and circulates cells in microfluidics channels, deviating target cells within an electric field (Hu et al., 2005; Landry et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Hu et al., 2005 and Landry et al., 2015.

claim: The concept of adding particles to individual live cells may open the door to novel strategies where other actionable properties such as fluorescence, electron density, scattering, plasmon resonance, thermal capacity, or electrical properties can be exploited.
source: The application we introduced here is focused on magnetic separation, but the same concept of adding particles to individual live cells may open the door to novel strategies where other actionable properties can be exploited in a simple and straightforward manner. For example, fluorescence or electron density can be manipulated on single cells (Binan et al., 2016), and recent advances in cellular nanotechnologies such as scattering and plasmon resonance using gold nanoparticles, thermal capacity with nanoshells, or electrical properties using carbon nanotubes can now be modulated only on chosen cells using low-cost commercially available reagents.
evidence: This is a speculative claim about future applications, with one citation to Binan et al., 2016.

claim: scMOCa allows isolation of live cells without previous knowledge of surface markers and can be based on morphological traits such as the presence of nuclear foci or lipid vesicles and the number of nuclei.
source: ScMOCa presents critical advantages over more traditional sorting techniques. It allows isolation of live cells without previous knowledge of surface markers and can simply be based on morphological traits such as the presence of nuclear foci or lipid vesicles and the number nuclei.
evidence: This claim is stated in the discussion and is supported by the experimental data presented in the Results section.

claim: scMOCa has the potential to sort based on time-dependent characteristics such as migration speed or foci resolution.
source: More importantly, it has the potential to sort based on time-dependent characteristics such as migration speed or foci resolution.
evidence: This claim is stated in the discussion and is supported by the experimental demonstration of sorting based on foci resolution.

claim: Because sorting is carried out in small chambers of similar size using scMOCa, there is no sample dilution.
source: In addition, because sorting is carried out in small chambers of similar size, there is no sample dilution.
evidence: This is stated as an advantage of the method based on its design.

claim: scMOCa prevents cells from sustaining strong shear stress upon passing through microfluidic tubing.
source: This prevents cells from sustaining strong shear stress upon passing through microfluidic tubing (Miltenyi et al., 1990), and allows their use in downstream applications such as cell culture, reinjection, or even lysis prior to transcriptomic or proteomic analysis.
evidence: This is stated as an advantage of the method, with a citation to Miltenyi et al., 1990.

source: Simplicity is a key advantage of scMOCa, as it does not require highly specialized software, or hardware such as microfluidic chips.

source: Indeed, a standard confocal microscope with no modification, simple handmade chambers and low-cost magnets are all that is needed to sort single cells of choice from among tens of thousands.
evidence: This is stated as an advantage of the method and is supported by the detailed protocol provided.

This operation effectively crosslinks biotin molecules to plasma membranes and was repeated for all targeted cells.
